{"candidate_slot":0,"current_prompt":"You are matching a system inventory to a supplied list of CVE advisories. The input is JSON with two parts: system_profile (installed products and versions) and advisories (each with an ID, a description, and affected-product information).

For each advisory, decide whether it applies to the installed system, applying the following steps in order.

STEP 1 — PRODUCT MATCH: Identify which product the advisory concerns using the affected information and description. Product names appear under many conventions: package-manager names, repository names, underscored or hyphenated names, and upstream/vendor names may all refer to the same product. Normalize names before comparing: strip vendor prefixes, convert underscores/hyphens to spaces, expand or match short names to full names, compare case-insensitively. If the product is not installed under ANY plausible alias, the advisory does not apply. But do not reject an advisory merely because its naming convention differs from the system profile's — check all aliases first. Conversely, never include an advisory for a product that is not installed just because its name resembles an installed one; verify a genuine alias relationship (e.g., 'repo/openssl' and 'openssl' match; 'libcrypto' and 'openssl' do not automatically).

STEP 2 — VERSION BOUNDS: Compare the installed version against the affected range, whether bounds appear in structured fields or in prose in the description:
- If the installed version is inside the affected range (inclusive of stated bounds unless explicitly excluded), the advisory applies.
- If the installed version is above the fixed/upper bound, the advisory does NOT apply — do not include it just because the product is installed.
- If the installed version is below a stated lower bound that starts the affected range, the advisory does NOT apply.
- If the affected range has no upper bound (e.g., 'all versions prior to X'), only the lower/starting condition matters.
- Compare versions NUMERICALLY segment by segment (1.2.10 > 1.2.9; 1.10 > 1.9), never lexicographically. Handle differing segment counts correctly: missing trailing segments are treated as zero (2.1 == 2.1.0) unless the advisory states otherwise. Versions just above a lower bound, just below a fixed version, or between a lower bound and a fix ARE affected — include them.
- When a bound is expressed only in prose, parse it exactly: 'prior to 3.2.1' means < 3.2.1; 'through 3.2.1' means <= 3.2.1; 'versions 2.0 to 2.5' usually means inclusive; 'before X' excludes X; 'X and later' includes X.
- Multi-segment versions (3-5 segments) are common: recompute each comparison a second time digit by digit before deciding. A frequent error is lexicographic mistakes on long versions (e.g., 1.2.10 vs 1.2.9, or 1.10.x vs 1.9.x).

STEP 3 — EXPLICIT EXCLUSIONS, checked precisely:
(a) List every exclusion in the advisory: 'not affected' sub-ranges, excluded version lists, 'fixed in Z' versions, 'only versions between A and B' qualifiers.
(b) Compare the INSTALLED version against each exclusion exactly, segment by segment, numerically. If the installed version equals an excluded version or falls inside an excluded sub-range, the advisory does NOT apply for that exclusion only.
(c) If the installed version is inside the general affected range but matches NO exclusion, the advisory DOES apply. The mere presence of excluded versions never excludes a different installed version.
(d) Beware of near-matches: installed 2.1.5 vs excluded 2.15, installed 1.2.0 vs excluded 1.2 — these are NOT the same version; compare exactly. Only a true numeric match excludes. Also beware the reverse error: an installed version that differs from a FIX version by only a trailing segment (e.g., installed 4.2.1.3 vs fixed 4.2.1.4) is still affected and must be included.

STEP 4 — MISSED ADVISORIES: Check EVERY advisory in the list, one by one, especially: prose-only or unusual bound formats; multi-segment versions requiring careful numeric comparison; installed versions above a stated lower bound but below a fix (these are the most frequently missed applicable cases); installed versions exactly on an inclusive bound; product names using vendor-stripped, underscore-to-space, repository-name, or other alias conventions. Verify each candidate inclusion AND each candidate exclusion at least twice before finalizing. If the product matches under any alias and the version satisfies the affected range with no matching exclusion, INCLUDE the advisory even if it seems borderline — a correct borderline inclusion is as important as a correct exclusion. Do not skip advisories whose bounds must be read from the description text; parse them literally.

STEP 5 — AMBIGUITY: If bounds are genuinely ambiguous, include only when the installed version is most plausibly within the affected range; otherwise exclude. Never invent CVE IDs — use only identifiers present in the supplied advisories list, and return each applicable ID exactly once.

Return ONLY a JSON object of the form {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} containing unique IDs from the supplied list. If none apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}. Output no other
